summary.text: Justinian I, also known as Justinian the Great, was Roman emperor from 527 to 565.
His reign aimed at a restoration of the Empire, which was only partly realised through the recovery of territories of the defunct Western Roman Empire.
He is remembered for rewriting Roman law as the Corpus Juris Civilis, still the basis of civil law in many modern states, and for a building program that produced the Hagia Sophia.

facts.label: Nickname
facts.value: "The emperor who never sleeps", for his work habits

facts.label: Western revenue gain
facts.value: Over a million solidi a year after his campaigns

facts.label: Law code
facts.value: The Corpus Juris Civilis, still a base of modern civil law

facts.label: Empress
facts.value: Theodora, who became very influential in politics

items.prompt: How well did Justinian's plan to restore the empire work out?

options.label: It fully succeeded, and the whole Western empire returned
It was only partly realised, with North Africa, Italy and southern Spain regained
It failed, since no western land was ever recovered
It succeeded in the west but lost the east to Persia

items.explain: The ambition of a restoration of the Empire was only partly realised. Generals conquered the Vandal Kingdom and the Ostrogothic Kingdom, and southern Spain was reclaimed.

items.prompt: A law student finds that her country's civil law rests on a uniform rewriting of Roman law made under one emperor. Which work is the root?

options.label: The Corpus Juris Civilis
The Tetrarchy
The Nika code
The renovatio imperii

items.explain: One of the most enduring parts of Justinian's legacy was the uniform rewriting of Roman law as the Corpus Juris Civilis, still the basis of civil law in many modern states.

items.prompt: Justinian came from a peasant family yet became emperor. What opened the path?

options.label: He won a string of victories over Persia and was crowned by the army
He married into the old Roman senate and inherited its offices
His uncle Justin adopted him, brought him to the capital, and later became emperor
He overthrew Emperor Anastasius and set up his own court

items.explain: Justin adopted Justinian, brought him to Constantinople and saw to his education. When Justin became emperor, Justinian helped and later became de facto ruler, then co-emperor and sole ruler.

items.prompt: Around 525 Justinian married Theodora, an actress, although he could not have done so in earlier times because of her class. What changed?

options.label: The senate voted her a title of nobility
Theodora gave up acting and entered the church
Justinian was crowned and ruled by his own law
His uncle, Emperor Justin I, lifted restrictions on such marriages

items.explain: In earlier times Justinian could not have married her, but his uncle Emperor Justin I had lifted restrictions on marriages with ex-actresses.

items.prompt: A historian praises Justinian as a great emperor but says his rule was not smooth. What does she cite?

options.label: A Persian king took his throne and held it for several years
The Nika riots nearly cost him the throne, and a plot on his life was found
Justin recovered and forced Justinian to step aside in disgrace
The Tzani people rose up and overthrew him from the Black Sea coast

items.explain: His rule was not universally popular. Early in his reign he nearly lost his throne during the Nika riots, and a conspiracy against his life was discovered as late as 562.

items.prompt: While Justinian reached for the West, a second war flared with Sasanian Persia in the east. How are the two connected?

options.label: Persia attacked after his western generals were killed
Persia was his ally in the war against the Ostrogoths
The second war was partly started by his ambitions in the west
Persia demanded the lands he took from the Vandals

items.explain: He fought the Sasanian Empire under Kavad I and later under Khosrow I, and the second conflict was partially initiated by his ambitions in the west.
